question: A student cannot clearly see objects placed at a distance but can read a book comfortably. The defect in the eye is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is myopia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Myopia, also called short-sightedness or near-sightedness, is the defect in which a person can see nearby objects clearly (can read a book) but cannot see distant objects clearly. (निकट दृष्टि दोष — दूर की वस्तु साफ नहीं दिखती)

 

• It occurs because the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina, either because the eyeball is too long or the eye lens is too curved (excessive converging power).

 

• Myopia is corrected by using spectacles with a concave (diverging) lens of suitable focal length, which diverges the incoming rays before they enter the eye.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): the image forms behind the retina; corrected using a convex lens.

 

• Presbyopia: an age-related defect where the eye's power of accommodation decreases; corrected using bifocal lenses.

 

• Astigmatism: occurs when the cornea is not perfectly spherical, causing blurred vision at all distances; corrected using a cylindrical lens.

 

• The normal human eye has a near point of about 25 cm and a far point at infinity.

 

NOTE

 

• astigmatism (Option A): A defect of unequal curvature of the cornea, not related to near/far focusing distance.

 

• hypermetropia (Option B): The opposite defect — distant objects are seen clearly but near objects (like a book) are not.

 

• presbyopia (Option D): Occurs due to ageing and affects near vision, but is not the cause described here (loss of near-point accommodation with age, not a permanent eyeball defect).

question: Which of the following statements is correct?
option_1: The size of the nucleus is large as compared to the size of the atom.
option_2: The electrons revolve around the nucleus in triangular paths.
option_3: The electrons do not revolve around the nucleus in circular paths.
option_4: Electrons have much smaller mass than protons and neutrons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Electrons have much smaller mass than protons and neutrons.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The mass of an electron is about 1/1837 times the mass of a proton, making it negligibly small compared to protons and neutrons. (इलेक्ट्रॉन का द्रव्यमान प्रोटॉन/न्यूट्रॉन से बहुत कम)

 

• The mass number of an atom is taken as the sum of protons and neutrons only, because the electron's contribution to mass is considered negligible.

 

• The nucleus is extremely small compared to the overall size of the atom — the atom is mostly empty space, as shown by Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rutherford's model proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths (orbits), similar to planets around the sun.

 

• Proton (charge +1, mass ≈ 1 u) and neutron (charge 0, mass ≈ 1 u) reside inside the nucleus; electron (charge −1, mass ≈ 1/1837 u) revolves outside it.

 

• J.J. Thomson discovered the electron (1897); Rutherford discovered the proton and the nucleus; James Chadwick discovered the neutron (1932).

 

NOTE

 

• The size of the nucleus is large... (Option A): Incorrect — the nucleus occupies only a tiny fraction of the atom's total volume.

 

• Electrons revolve...triangular paths (Option B): Incorrect — as per Rutherford/Bohr's model, electrons revolve in circular paths.

 

• Electrons do not revolve...circular paths (Option C): Incorrect — this contradicts the accepted atomic model in which electrons do revolve in circular orbits.

question: Two objects are being accelerated — one has a mass of 3 kg and is accelerated at 4 m/s², and the other has a mass of 5 kg and is accelerated at 2 m/s². Which one needs a greater force to move?
option_2: It cannot be determined without knowing the distance
solution_text:
The correct answer is The 3 kg object.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's second law of motion, Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma). (न्यूटन का द्वितीय नियम — बल = द्रव्यमान × त्वरण)

 

• Force on the 3 kg object = 3 × 4 = 12 N.

 

• Force on the 5 kg object = 5 × 2 = 10 N.

 

• Since 12 N > 10 N, the 3 kg object requires the greater force.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of force is the newton (N), where 1 N is the force needed to give a 1 kg mass an acceleration of 1 m/s².

 

• Newton's second law can also be written as F = dp/dt, the rate of change of momentum.

 

• Force is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.

 

NOTE

 

• Both require the same force (Option A): Incorrect, since the computed forces (12 N and 10 N) are different.

 

• It cannot be determined without knowing the distance (Option B): Incorrect — force depends only on mass and acceleration, not distance, as per F = ma.

 

• The 5 kg object (Option D): Incorrect — although it has greater mass, its smaller acceleration makes its net force (10 N) smaller than that on the 3 kg object (12 N).

question: Now a days, which of the following petroleum products is used in place of coal-tar for metalling the roads?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bitumen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bitumen is a black, sticky, highly viscous petroleum product that is now commonly used instead of coal-tar for road metalling (asphalting roads). (बिटुमेन — सड़क निर्माण में प्रयुक्त)

 

• It is obtained as a residue during the fractional distillation of petroleum (crude oil) at the refinery, from the fraction left after all lighter fractions are removed.

 

• Bitumen provides good binding strength and water resistance, making roads durable, and it is cheaper and more consistent in quality than coal-tar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fractional distillation of petroleum yields, in order of increasing boiling point: petroleum gas, petrol (gasoline), kerosene, diesel, lubricating oil, and bitumen/paraffin wax as residue.

 

• Coal-tar is a by-product of the destructive distillation of coal (used to make coke), and was traditionally used in road-laying before bitumen became common.

 

• Paraffin wax, another petroleum product, is used to make candles, packaging and vaseline.

 

NOTE

 

• Naphthalene (Option A): A coal-tar derivative used in mothballs and as a raw material for dyes, not for road construction.

 

• Coke (Option B): A solid residue from destructive distillation of coal, used mainly as a fuel and reducing agent in blast furnaces.

 

• Paraffin wax (Option C): A petroleum product used for candles and waterproof coatings, not for metalling roads.

question: Which of the following is a common use of baking soda?
option_2: Reacting with alcohol to make soap
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neutralising excess stomach acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Baking soda, chemically sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), is a mild base and is commonly used as an antacid to neutralise excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach, giving relief from acidity and heartburn. (सोडियम बाइकार्बोनेट — अम्लता से राहत)

 

• The reaction is: NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂, which consumes the excess acid and produces harmless products.

 

• It is prepared industrially by the Solvay process, using sodium chloride, ammonia and carbon dioxide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Baking soda is also used in baking as a leavening (rising) agent, since heating it releases CO₂ gas which makes dough/cake rise.

 

• It is a key ingredient of baking powder, along with a mild edible acid such as tartaric acid.

 

• Baking soda is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers and as a mild cleaning/deodorising agent.

 

NOTE

 

• Preventing bacterial decomposition (Option A): Not a typical use of baking soda; preservation from bacteria is usually done using salt, sugar, or chemical preservatives like sodium benzoate.

 

• Reacting with alcohol to make soap (Option B): Soap is made by reacting fats/oils with sodium hydroxide (NaOH), not baking soda, in a process called saponification.

 

• Increasing acidity in soil beds (Option D): Baking soda is a base, so it would decrease acidity, not increase it; agricultural lime (calcium compounds) is used to reduce soil acidity.

question: What type of bonding exists in most organic compounds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Covalent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Most organic compounds (compounds of carbon) are held together by covalent bonds, in which atoms share pairs of electrons. (सहसंयोजक बंधन — कार्बनिक यौगिकों में)

 

• Carbon has 4 valence electrons and forms 4 covalent bonds, allowing it to bond with other carbon atoms and elements like hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen, forming stable chains, branches and rings.

 

• Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points, are usually poor conductors of electricity, and are often soluble in organic solvents rather than water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Catenation, the property of carbon to form bonds with other carbon atoms, is responsible for the huge number and diversity of organic compounds.

 

• A covalent bond formed by sharing of a single pair of electrons is a single bond; two pairs form a double bond, and three pairs form a triple bond (as in ethane, ethene and ethyne respectively).

 

• Ionic compounds (such as NaCl), by contrast, are typically formed between metals and non-metals through transfer of electrons.

 

NOTE

 

• Ionic (Option B): Involves transfer of electrons between a metal and a non-metal; typical of inorganic salts, not carbon compounds.

 

• Coordinate (Option C): A special type of covalent bond where both shared electrons come from one atom; seen in some complex/organic molecules but not the dominant bond type overall.

 

• Metallic (Option D): Bonding found in metals, involving a 'sea of electrons'; not found in organic compounds.

question: What happens in a longitudinal wave?
option_1: Particles stay completely still as the wave passes
option_2: Particles move in circles around their rest position
option_3: Particles oscillate back and forth about their position of rest
option_4: Particles oscillate up and down about their mean position
solution_text:
The correct answer is Particles oscillate back and forth about their position of rest.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth (to and fro) parallel to (along) the direction of propagation of the wave. (अनुदैर्ध्य तरंग — कणों का कंपन तरंग की दिशा के समांतर)

 

• This to-and-fro motion creates alternate regions of compression (particles close together, high pressure) and rarefaction (particles far apart, low pressure) along the wave.

 

• Sound waves are the most common example of longitudinal waves and can travel through solids, liquids and gases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a transverse wave, particles oscillate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation (up and down), as seen in light waves and waves on a stretched string.

 

• Longitudinal waves are characterised by wavelength (distance between two consecutive compressions or rarefactions) and can be represented graphically by pressure/density variation.

 

• Water waves are a combination of both longitudinal and transverse motion (particles move in circular/elliptical paths).

 

NOTE

 

• Particles stay completely still (Option A): Incorrect — a wave, by definition, involves the disturbance/oscillation of particles of the medium.

 

• Particles move in circles (Option B): This describes surface water waves, not longitudinal sound waves.

 

• Particles oscillate up and down (Option D): This describes a transverse wave, not a longitudinal wave.

question: Which of the following is an enzyme that is secreted in the stomach during the process of digestion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pepsin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pepsin is the chief digestive enzyme secreted by the gastric glands of the stomach; it breaks down proteins into smaller peptides. (पेप्सिन — आमाशय में प्रोटीन का पाचन)

 

• Pepsin is secreted in an inactive form called pepsinogen, which is converted into active pepsin by hydrochloric acid (HCl) present in gastric juice.

 

• Pepsin works best in the highly acidic environment of the stomach (pH about 1.5–2.5), provided by HCl secreted by the oxyntic (parietal) cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gastric juice contains HCl, pepsin, and mucus; HCl kills bacteria in food and activates pepsinogen, while mucus protects the stomach lining from the acid.

 

• Other digestive enzymes: Amylase (saliva/pancreas) digests starch; Trypsin (pancreas) digests proteins in the small intestine; Lipase digests fats.

 

• Rennin, another stomach enzyme found mainly in infants, helps digest milk protein (casein).

 

NOTE

 

• Trypsin (Option A): A protein-digesting enzyme secreted by the pancreas, active in the small intestine, not the stomach.

 

• Mucus (Option C): Not an enzyme; it is a protective secretion that shields the stomach lining from the corrosive action of HCl and pepsin.

 

• Amylase (Option D): A carbohydrate-digesting enzyme found in saliva and pancreatic juice, not the stomach (the stomach does not secrete amylase).

question: A gun fires a bullet horizontally. Which of the following statements is correct?
option_2: The gun experiences a smaller backward force than the bullet's forward force.
option_3: The bullet exerts no force on the gun.
option_4: The gun experiences a backward force equal to the forward force on the bullet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The gun experiences a backward force equal to the forward force on the bullet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This situation is explained by Newton's third law of motion: for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. (न्यूटन का तृतीय नियम — क्रिया और प्रतिक्रिया)

 

• When the gun exerts a forward force on the bullet, the bullet exerts an equal and opposite backward force on the gun, causing the gun to recoil.

 

• This is also an application of the law of conservation of momentum: the total momentum of the gun-bullet system before firing (zero) equals the total momentum after firing, so the backward momentum of the gun equals the forward momentum of the bullet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Since the mass of the gun is much greater than the mass of the bullet, the gun's recoil velocity is much smaller than the bullet's velocity, even though the momentum (and force) magnitudes are equal.

 

• Newton's third law forces act on two different bodies (gun and bullet) simultaneously and never cancel each other out.

 

• Other everyday examples of Newton's third law: walking (foot pushes ground backward, ground pushes foot forward), swimming, and rocket propulsion.

 

NOTE

 

• Recoil depends on gravity (Option A): Incorrect — recoil arises from momentum conservation/Newton's third law, not gravity.

 

• The gun experiences a smaller backward force (Option B): Incorrect — by Newton's third law the forces are always equal in magnitude (though the resulting accelerations differ due to different masses).

 

• The bullet exerts no force on the gun (Option C): Incorrect — the bullet does exert a force on the gun; this is precisely what causes recoil.

question: A car with a mass of 150 kg is moving at a speed of 36 km/hr. What is the amount of work required to increase its speed to 72 km/hr?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 22,500 J.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By the work-energy theorem, the work done on a body equals its change in kinetic energy: W = ΔKE = ½m(v² − u²). (कार्य-ऊर्जा प्रमेय — कार्य = गतिज ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन)

 

• First convert both speeds from km/hr to m/s using the factor 5/18: u = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s, and v = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s.

 

• Now apply the formula: W = ½ × 150 × (20² − 10²) = 75 × (400 − 100) = 75 × 300 = 22,500 J.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion; KE = ½mv², measured in joules (J).

 

• Work is said to be done when a force produces a displacement in the direction of the force: W = F × d, also measured in joules. 1 joule = 1 newton-metre.

 

• Power is the rate of doing work, P = W/t, measured in watts (W); 1 watt = 1 joule/second. A commonly used commercial unit of energy is the kilowatt-hour (kWh), equal to 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

 

NOTE

 

• 37,500 J (Option A): A wrong-formula slip — using the full ½mv² for the final speed without correctly subtracting the initial KE.

 

• 7,500 J (Option B): Equals ½mu², i.e. only the initial kinetic energy, mistakenly taken as the answer.

 

• 30,000 J (Option D): Equals ½mv², i.e. only the final kinetic energy — the initial KE (7,500 J) was not subtracted.

question: Which rule helps determine the direction of the magnetic field inside a current-carrying loop?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right-hand thumb rule.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right-hand thumb rule (also called the Maxwell's right-hand grip rule) gives the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor or loop. (दक्षिण हस्त अंगूठा नियम — चुंबकीय क्षेत्र की दिशा)

 

• Statement: If a current-carrying conductor is held in the right hand such that the thumb points in the direction of current flow, then the direction in which the fingers curl gives the direction of the magnetic field lines.

 

• For a current-carrying loop, curling the fingers of the right hand in the direction of current flow makes the thumb point in the direction of the magnetic field at the centre of the loop.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the force (motion) on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field — used in electric motors.

 

• Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of the induced current in a conductor moving in a magnetic field — used in electric generators (based on electromagnetic induction).

 

• A solenoid (a coil of many circular turns) behaves like a bar magnet, with field lines emerging from one end (north pole) and entering the other (south pole), also found using the right-hand thumb rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Fleming's right-hand rule (Option A): Used for finding the direction of induced current in a generator, not the magnetic field due to a current.

 

• Left-hand thumb rule (Option B): Not a standard named rule in this context; the standard rule for force direction is Fleming's left-hand rule.

 

• Fleming's left-hand rule (Option D): Used for finding the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (motor effect), not the field due to current.

question: If you apply pressure to a gas, what happens to the intermolecular spaces and forces?
option_1: Intermolecular spaces decrease, intermolecular forces increase.
option_2: Intermolecular spaces increase, intermolecular forces decrease.
option_3: Intermolecular spaces and forces both increase.
option_4: Both intermolecular spaces and forces remain unchanged.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intermolecular spaces decrease, intermolecular forces increase.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gases have particles that are far apart with weak intermolecular forces, and gases are highly compressible. (गैस — दाब बढ़ाने पर अंतराआण्विक दूरी घटती है)

 

• When pressure is applied to a gas, its particles are pushed closer together, so the intermolecular space decreases.

 

• As the particles come closer, the intermolecular forces of attraction increase, since these forces are inversely related to the distance between particles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The states of matter in order of increasing intermolecular force and decreasing intermolecular space are: gas < liquid < solid.

 

• Boyle's Law states that at constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed amount of gas is inversely proportional to its volume (P ∝ 1/V) — a direct consequence of decreasing intermolecular space under pressure.

 

• Gases can be liquefied by applying high pressure and low temperature, which brings molecules close enough for stronger attractive forces to dominate (e.g. LPG, CNG).

 

NOTE

 

• Intermolecular spaces increase, forces decrease (Option B): This is the opposite of what happens on applying pressure — pressure compresses the gas, not expands it.

 

• Both increase (Option C): Incorrect — spaces decrease, not increase, when pressure is applied.

 

• Both remain unchanged (Option D): Incorrect — gases are highly compressible, so applying pressure clearly changes both spacing and forces.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about plant's response to environmental stimulus?
option_1: Plants have very weak muscles to respond environmental stimulus.
option_2: Plants have special connective tissues to receive environmental stimulus.
option_3: Plants have very fine nerves to receive environmental stimulus.
option_4: Some plants can respond to the stimulus of touch.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Some plants can respond to the stimulus of touch.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Unlike animals, plants lack a nervous system, muscles and nerves, yet certain plants can respond to touch through changes in turgor pressure (water pressure inside cells). (स्पर्शानुवर्तन — छुई-मुई का पौधा)

 

• The classic example is Mimosa pudica (the touch-me-not or 'chhui-mui' plant), whose leaves fold up immediately when touched, due to a rapid loss of water from cells at the base of the leaflets (pulvinus).

 

• Sundew and Venus flytrap (insectivorous plants) also show a touch response, closing their leaves to trap insects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plant movements caused by external stimuli are called tropisms when directional (e.g. phototropism — towards light, geotropism/gravitropism — towards gravity, hydrotropism — towards water) and nasties when non-directional (e.g. the touch response of Mimosa, called thigmonasty or seismonasty).

 

• Plant responses are coordinated by chemical messengers called plant hormones (phytohormones) — e.g. auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic acid and ethylene — not by nerves.

 

• Auxin is responsible for the bending of a shoot towards light (phototropism), by promoting faster cell elongation on the shaded side.

 

NOTE

 

• Plants have very weak muscles... (Option A): Incorrect — plants have no muscles at all; their movement is due to changes in turgor pressure, not muscular contraction.

 

• Plants have special connective tissues... (Option B): Incorrect — connective tissue is an animal tissue type; plants do not possess it.

 

• Plants have very fine nerves... (Option C): Incorrect — plants have no nervous system or nerves; they respond via hormones and turgor changes.

question:
White light is incident obliquely on a glass prism, which of the following statement(s) is/are true?

(i) Red colour undergoes maximum deviation.

(ii) The speed of violet colour is the least while travelling through the prism.

(iii) The refractive index of violet is minimum.

(iv) The refractive index of red is minimum.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both (ii) and (iv).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When white light passes through a prism, it splits into its constituent colours (dispersion), because each colour travels at a different speed inside glass and hence bends by a different amount. (प्रिज्म में वर्ण विक्षेपण — बैंगनी सबसे अधिक विचलित)

 

• Violet light has the shortest wavelength, so it slows down the most inside glass, giving it the highest refractive index and hence it undergoes maximum deviation. So statement (ii) — violet has the least speed — is correct.

 

• Red light has the longest wavelength, travels fastest inside the glass among visible colours, and has the minimum refractive index, so it deviates the least. So statement (iv) — red has minimum refractive index — is correct.

 

• Statement (i) is false because red undergoes minimum, not maximum, deviation; statement (iii) is false because violet has the maximum, not minimum, refractive index.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The order of deviation (increasing) of colours through a prism follows the mnemonic VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) — violet deviates the most, red the least.

 

• Refractive index (n) = speed of light in vacuum / speed of light in medium; a higher refractive index means a lower speed in that medium.

 

• A rainbow is formed by the dispersion, total internal reflection and refraction of sunlight through water droplets in the atmosphere.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, C and D are incorrect because each pairs at least one false statement — (i) and (iii) are both false, since it is violet (not red) that deviates the most, and violet's refractive index is the maximum (not minimum).

question: The method of extraction of a metal depends on its:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Position in the reactivity series.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The method used to extract a metal from its ore depends on the metal's reactivity, i.e., its position in the activity/reactivity series. (धातु निष्कर्षण — सक्रियता श्रेणी पर निर्भर)

 

• Highly reactive metals (like Na, K, Ca, Mg, Al) are extracted by electrolytic reduction of their molten (fused) compounds, since they cannot be reduced by ordinary reducing agents.

 

• Metals of medium reactivity (like Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu) are extracted by reduction of their oxides using carbon/other reducing agents (e.g. in a blast furnace).

 

• Metals of low reactivity (like Au, Ag, Pt, Cu) occur in a free (native) state, or are extracted by simple heating/methods that require little energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The activity series (in decreasing order of reactivity): K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > (H) > Cu > Ag > Au.

 

• Metallurgy is the process of extracting metals from their ores; it broadly involves crushing, concentration of ore, reduction, and refining.

 

• Extraction of highly reactive metals is energy-intensive, which is why aluminium extraction (Hall-Héroult process) requires large amounts of electricity.

 

NOTE

 

• Mass number (Option A): Relates to the number of protons + neutrons in a nucleus; not the basis for choosing an extraction method.

 

• Colour (Option B): A physical property of a metal that has no bearing on how it is extracted from its ore.

 

• Atomic number (Option C): The number of protons in an atom; while related to identity, it is the metal's chemical reactivity — not its atomic number directly — that determines the extraction method used.

question: A block exerts a thrust of 500 N on a surface of area 0.25 m². The pressure exerted by the block is _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2000 N/m².

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pressure is defined as the thrust (force) acting normally per unit area: Pressure = Force ÷ Area. (दाब = बल / क्षेत्रफल)

 

• Here, thrust F = 500 N and area A = 0.25 m².

 

• Pressure = 500 ÷ 0.25 = 2000 N/m².

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa), where 1 Pa = 1 N/m². Other common units include the bar, atmosphere (atm) and mm of Hg.

 

• For the same thrust, pressure is inversely proportional to area — this is why a sharp knife (small area) cuts more easily than a blunt one, and why wide tyres or snow shoes reduce sinking by spreading the force over a larger area.

 

• Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa, and is measured using a barometer.

 

NOTE

 

• 125 N/m² (Option B): Obtained by wrongly multiplying force and area (500 × 0.25 = 125) instead of dividing.

 

• 500 N/m² (Option C): The thrust value taken directly as the pressure, ignoring the area altogether.

 

• 250 N/m² (Option D): Obtained from an incorrect division (e.g. 500 ÷ 2), not the given area of 0.25 m².

question: In the process of sexual reproduction in flowering plants, what is the primary role of the pistil?
option_3: Receives pollen and houses the ovules for fertilisation
solution_text:
The correct answer is Receives pollen and houses the ovules for fertilisation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The pistil (gynoecium) is the female reproductive part of a flower; it receives pollen grains on its stigma and contains the ovules (which develop into seeds after fertilisation) inside the ovary. (स्त्रीकेसर — मादा जनन अंग)

 

• The pistil has three main parts: the stigma (sticky tip that receives pollen), the style (tube connecting stigma to ovary), and the ovary (base, containing ovules).

 

• After pollination, the pollen tube grows down through the style, carrying male gametes to the ovule inside the ovary, where fertilisation occurs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The stamen (androecium) is the male reproductive part of the flower, consisting of the anther (produces pollen grains) and filament (stalk supporting the anther).

 

• Colourful petals (corolla) attract pollinators like insects and birds, aiding cross-pollination.

 

• After fertilisation, the ovary develops into a fruit, and the ovules develop into seeds.

 

NOTE

 

• Produces pollen grains (Option A): This is the role of the anther (part of the stamen), not the pistil.

 

• Attracts pollinators with colorful petals (Option B): This is the function of the corolla (petals), not the pistil.

 

• Supports the flower with nutrients (Option D): This is not a specific function of the pistil; nutrients are supplied through the plant's vascular tissue generally.

question: Which statement is INCORRECT about a household electric circuit?
option_1: A fuse is always connected in the live wire.
option_2: A fuse protects the circuit from excessive current.
option_3: Current through each appliance is the same.
option_4: All appliances are connected in parallel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Current through each appliance is the same.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a household electric circuit, all appliances are connected in parallel, so that each appliance gets the same voltage but the current drawn by each can be different, depending on its resistance/power rating. (घरेलू परिपथ — समांतर क्रम में जुड़े उपकरण)

 

• Since current I = V/R, and different appliances have different resistances, they draw different currents even though the voltage across each is the same — making the statement 'current through each appliance is the same' incorrect.

 

• Connecting appliances in parallel also ensures that if one appliance stops working (or is switched off), the others continue to function normally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• A fuse is a safety device made of a wire with a low melting point, connected in series with the live wire, which melts and breaks the circuit if the current exceeds a safe limit — protecting appliances from short-circuits/overloading.

 

• Standard household wiring in India supplies 220 V AC at 50 Hz, and typically uses three wires: live (red/brown), neutral (black/blue), and earth (green).

 

• Earthing (grounding) protects users from electric shock by providing a safe path for leakage current to flow to the ground.

 

NOTE

 

• A fuse is always connected in the live wire (Option A): This is a correct statement about household circuits, as it ensures the circuit is cut off immediately on overload.

 

• A fuse protects the circuit from excessive current (Option B): This is a correct statement — it is precisely the fuse's function.

 

• All appliances are connected in parallel (Option D): This is a correct statement about standard household wiring.

question: Which of the following can be considered a reason for Mendel's success in formulating laws of inheritance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is He was a well-trained scientist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gregor Johann Mendel is known as the 'Father of Genetics'; his success is attributed to his scientific, methodical approach — careful selection of the pea plant (Pisum sativum), controlled cross-breeding experiments, and statistical/mathematical analysis of results over several generations. (मेंडल — आनुवंशिकी के जनक)

 

• He was a well-trained scientist who applied rigorous, quantitative methods to biology — counting and analysing large numbers of offspring to derive his laws (Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation, Law of Independent Assortment).

 

• Mendel chose the garden pea plant because it has several easily observable contrasting traits (e.g. tall/dwarf, round/wrinkled seeds), a short life cycle, and can be both self-pollinated and cross-pollinated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendel presented his findings in 1865 in a paper titled 'Experiments on Plant Hybridization', but the significance of his work was not recognised until 1900, when it was independently rediscovered by de Vries, Correns and Tschermak.

 

• Mendel's Law of Dominance states that when two contrasting alleles are present, only the dominant one is expressed in the phenotype.

 

• The F1 generation in a monohybrid cross shows a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation.

 

NOTE

 

• He had supernatural power (Option A): Not a real or scientific reason; Mendel's success came from careful experimentation, not any supernatural ability.

 

• He had knowledge of mathmatics (Option B): While mathematics helped him analyse ratios, this alone (without a genuine trained scientific method) is not considered the primary reason for his success as commonly stated.

 

• He was a monk (Option D): Though Mendel was indeed an Augustinian monk, this was incidental to his scientific success, which is credited to his rigorous experimental approach rather than his religious vocation.

question: Bohr's model is only applicable to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is hydrogen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bohr's atomic model (proposed by Niels Bohr in 1913) was developed and is strictly applicable only to hydrogen and hydrogen-like species — i.e., single-electron systems such as H, He⁺, Li²⁺, Be³⁺. (बोर मॉडल — केवल हाइड्रोजन जैसे एक-इलेक्ट्रॉन परमाणुओं के लिए)

 

• For neutral hydrogen (H), which has just one electron and one proton, Bohr's model successfully explains the atomic spectrum using discrete, quantised circular orbits (energy levels).

 

• Bohr's model fails to accurately explain the spectra of multi-electron atoms (like neutral He, Li, or Be) because it does not account for electron-electron repulsion, which requires more advanced quantum mechanical models.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bohr postulated that electrons revolve in fixed, quantised circular orbits (stationary states) without radiating energy, and that energy is absorbed or emitted only when an electron jumps between orbits.

 

• The quantum mechanical model (Schrödinger's model), developed later, successfully explains the structure of multi-electron atoms using probability-based electron clouds (orbitals).

 

• Hydrogen-like ions (H, He⁺, Li²⁺) each have only one electron, so Bohr's model can still be applied to them, even though they are ions of higher-Z elements.

 

NOTE

 

• beryllium (Option A): A multi-electron neutral atom (4 electrons); Bohr's model cannot accurately describe it.

 

• lithium (Option B): A multi-electron neutral atom (3 electrons); not correctly explained by Bohr's simple model.

 

• helium (Option D): A multi-electron neutral atom (2 electrons); Bohr's model does not work for neutral helium (though it does work for the He⁺ ion, which has only 1 electron).

question: In which part of the female reproductive system is the egg fertilised by sperm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fallopian tube.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fertilisation — the fusion of the male gamete (sperm) with the female gamete (egg/ovum) — normally occurs in the Fallopian tube (oviduct) of the female reproductive system. (डिंबवाहिनी नली — निषेचन का स्थान)

 

• The egg released from the ovary during ovulation travels through the Fallopian tube, where sperm that have travelled up from the vagina through the uterus meet and fertilise it.

 

• After fertilisation, the resulting zygote continues to travel down the Fallopian tube and implants itself in the lining of the uterus, where it develops into an embryo.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries (produce eggs and hormones), a pair of Fallopian tubes, the uterus (where the embryo develops), and the vagina (birth canal).

 

• Each ovary releases one mature egg approximately every 28 days, a process called ovulation, as part of the menstrual cycle.

 

• If fertilisation does not occur, the thickened uterine lining breaks down and is shed as menstruation.

 

NOTE

 

• Vagina (Option A): The passage through which sperm enters the female body during copulation and through which the baby is delivered; not the site of fertilisation.

 

• Uterus (Option B): The site where the fertilised egg (embryo) implants and develops, not where fertilisation itself occurs.

 

• Ovary (Option D): The organ that produces and releases the egg (ovum), but fertilisation happens after the egg leaves the ovary, in the Fallopian tube.

question: During the Chlor-Alkali process, which of the following products is NOT obtained directly from the electrolysis of brine?
option_4: Sodium metal deposited at the cathode
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium metal deposited at the cathode.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chlor-Alkali process is the electrolysis of a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine), producing three useful products: chlorine gas at the anode, hydrogen gas at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution near the cathode. (क्लोर-क्षार प्रक्रम — सोडियम धातु नहीं बनता)

 

• At the cathode, since water is present, H₂ gas is liberated (not sodium metal) because water is preferentially reduced over the sodium ion under these conditions, leaving Na⁺ and OH⁻ ions in solution, which combine to form NaOH.

 

• At the anode, chloride ions are oxidised to form chlorine gas (Cl₂).

 

• Sodium metal cannot be obtained this way — it is instead obtained by the electrolysis of molten (fused) sodium chloride (Down's process), where there is no water to compete with the sodium ion at the cathode.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uses of the three Chlor-Alkali products: NaOH — in soap and detergent manufacture; Cl₂ — in PVC, disinfectants (bleaching powder) and water purification; H₂ — as a fuel and in the manufacture of ammonia (Haber process).

 

• Bleaching powder (CaOCl₂) is manufactured by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime (Ca(OH)₂).

 

• Washing soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) is obtained by treating sodium hydroxide solution with carbon dioxide.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrogen gas at the cathode (Option A): This IS correctly obtained from the electrolysis of brine, so it is not the answer being asked for.

 

• Sodium hydroxide solution (Option B): This IS correctly obtained (accumulates near the cathode) in the Chlor-Alkali process.

 

• Chlorine gas at the anode (Option C): This IS correctly obtained from the electrolysis of brine, at the anode.

question: When touching a hot object with the hand, human beings are able to remove their hand immediately because:
option_1: human beings are sensitive to the stimulus of touch
option_2: human beings are the supreme creatures of the living world
option_3: every living organism can do so
option_4: human beings are more intelligent than others
solution_text:
The correct answer is human beings are sensitive to the stimulus of touch.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Human beings are able to withdraw their hand almost instantly from a hot object because of a reflex action, which occurs due to the sensitivity of the skin's touch receptors to heat/pain stimuli. (प्रतिवर्ती क्रिया — स्पर्श उद्दीपन के प्रति संवेदनशीलता)

 

• The sequence is: receptor (skin) → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector (muscle), forming a reflex arc. This pathway does not wait for a decision from the brain, making the response extremely fast.

 

• This quick, involuntary reaction is a protective mechanism to prevent tissue damage from prolonged exposure to a harmful (hot) stimulus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• A reflex arc is the shortest, quickest neural pathway from receptor to effector, bypassing conscious processing in the brain for a faster response.

 

• The spinal cord acts as the coordinating centre for many reflex actions (like the knee-jerk reflex, withdrawal from a hot/sharp object).

 

• After a reflex response, the sensory information does still reach the brain (via the spinal cord), which is why we consciously feel the pain shortly after withdrawing the hand.

 

NOTE

 

• human beings are the supreme creatures... (Option B): An irrelevant, non-scientific statement; it does not explain the mechanism behind this rapid response.

 

• every living organism can do so (Option C): Incorrect — not every organism has the same nervous system or reflex mechanism to remove a body part from a stimulus in this manner.

 

• human beings are more intelligent than others (Option D): Irrelevant — this reflex response is involuntary and does not depend on intelligence, but on the nervous system's reflex pathway.

question: Which non-metal exhibits a lustrous shine like metals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iodine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Although most non-metals are dull in appearance, iodine is an exception — it is a lustrous (shiny), greyish-black solid that resembles a metal in its physical appearance. (आयोडीन — अधात्विक होते हुए भी चमकदार)

 

• On gentle heating, solid iodine directly changes into violet vapours without passing through the liquid state, a property known as sublimation.

 

• Despite its lustrous, metal-like appearance, iodine still exhibits typical non-metallic chemical properties, such as forming acidic oxides and being an electron acceptor (oxidising agent).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other exceptions where non-metals show unusual properties: carbon (in the form of graphite) conducts electricity, and diamond (also carbon) is the hardest known natural substance.

 

• General properties of non-metals include: they are usually dull, brittle (if solid), poor conductors of heat and electricity, and have low melting/boiling points compared to metals.

 

• Iodine is used as an antiseptic (tincture of iodine) and is essential for the functioning of the thyroid gland (in the hormone thyroxine).

 

NOTE

 

• Sulphur (Option A): A typical dull, brittle yellow non-metallic solid; does not show metallic lustre.

 

• Flourine (Option B): A pale yellow, highly reactive gas at room temperature; not lustrous.

 

• Chlorine (Option C): A greenish-yellow, pungent-smelling gas at room temperature; not lustrous.

question: Why does growth in plants occur only at specific regions?
option_1: Because all plant tissues can divide only once
option_2: Because permanent tissues keep dividing throughout the plant
option_3: Because all plant cells stop growing after maturity
option_4: Because meristematic tissues are located only in specific regions
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because meristematic tissues are located only in specific regions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Growth in plants is localised (restricted to specific regions) because only meristematic tissue — the tissue responsible for continuous cell division — is present at these specific growing points, unlike animals where growth is more generalised. (विभज्योतक ऊतक — पौधों में वृद्धि के विशिष्ट स्थान)

 

• Apical meristem, found at the tips of roots and shoots, is responsible for primary growth — increase in the length of the plant.

 

• Lateral (intercalary/cambial) meristem, found at the base of leaves/internodes and as the vascular cambium, is responsible for secondary growth — increase in girth (thickness) of stems/roots.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plant tissues are broadly classified as meristematic tissue (actively dividing, immature) and permanent tissue (differentiated, has lost the ability to divide, e.g. parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma).

 

• Cells produced by the apical meristem differentiate into three primary tissue systems: protoderm (gives rise to epidermis), procambium (gives rise to vascular tissue), and ground meristem (gives rise to ground tissue).

 

• Unlike plants, most animals show growth throughout the body during the growing phase, and growth generally stops after reaching maturity.

 

NOTE

 

• Because all plant tissues can divide only once (Option A): Incorrect and misleading — meristematic tissue can divide repeatedly throughout the plant's life, not just once.

 

• Because permanent tissues keep dividing... (Option B): Incorrect — by definition, permanent tissues have lost the capacity to divide; only meristematic tissue divides.

 

• Because all plant cells stop growing after maturity (Option C): Incorrect — this does not explain why growth is localised to specific regions in the first place.

question:
Pipe P can fill 4/5 part of a tank in 28 hours and pipe Q can fill 2/3 part of the same tank in 42 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 7 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 14 hours.

Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 45 hours.

 

GIVEN

 

• P fills 4/5 of the tank in 28 h; Q fills 2/3 of the tank in 42 h; P and Q run together for 7 h, then R alone empties that water in 14 h.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Time for P to fill the whole tank = 28 ÷ (4/5) = 28 × 5/4 = 35 h ⇒ P's rate = 1/35 tank/h.

 

• Time for Q to fill the whole tank = 42 ÷ (2/3) = 42 × 3/2 = 63 h ⇒ Q's rate = 1/63 tank/h.

 

• In 7 h, water filled by P and Q = 7 × (1/35 + 1/63) = 7 × (9/315 + 5/315) = 7 × 14/315 = 98/315 = 14/45 of the tank.

 

• R empties this 14/45 of the tank in 14 h ⇒ R's rate = (14/45) ÷ 14 = 1/45 tank/h (emptying, so rate = −1/45).

 

• Combined rate of P, Q, R = 1/35 + 1/63 − 1/45. LCM(35, 63, 45) = 315 ⇒ 9/315 + 5/315 − 7/315 = 7/315 = 1/45.

 

• So together they fill the tank in 45 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each pipe's given 'part in given time' to 'full tank time' first (divide time by the fraction). Then just add/subtract the unit rates (1/time) with a common LCM denominator — this avoids fraction confusion at every step.

 

NOTE

 

• A pipe that empties a tank is always given a negative rate when combined with filling pipes; don't forget the sign.

question: After selling an article at a discount of 37%, the profit percentage obtained is 50%. What is the mark-up percentage (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 138.10%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Discount = 37% on the marked price (MP); resulting profit = 50% on the cost price (CP).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let MP = 100. Selling price (SP) after 37% discount = 100 × (1 − 0.37) = 63.

 

• Given profit = 50% on CP, so SP = 1.5 × CP ⇒ CP = 63 ÷ 1.5 = 42.

 

• Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100 = [(100 − 42) ÷ 42] × 100 = (58 ÷ 42) × 100 = 5800/42 = 138.10% (to 2 decimal places).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Take MP = 100 always in mark-up/discount questions. SP = MP(1 − d%), CP = SP/(1 + p%). Mark-up% = (MP − CP)/CP × 100 — a single chain of substitutions gets you there fast.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse mark-up % (calculated on CP) with discount % (calculated on MP) — they use different bases, which is exactly why the mark-up % here (138.10%) looks much larger than the discount (37%).

question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 50 km/hr and 90 km/hr. The length of one train is 430 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 31 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, rounded off to 2 decimal places, is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 775.56 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Speeds: 50 km/hr and 90 km/hr, opposite directions; length of one train = 430 m; time to cross each other = 31 s.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Relative speed (opposite directions ⇒ speeds add) = 50 + 90 = 140 km/hr = 140 × 5/18 = 350/9 m/s.

 

• When two trains cross each other, total distance covered = sum of their lengths.

 

• Total distance = relative speed × time = (350/9) × 31 = 10850/9 = 1205.56 m (approx).

 

• Length of other train = Total distance − 430 = 1205.56 − 430 = 775.56 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert km/hr to m/s using ×5/18; for two trains crossing each other, always use (sum of lengths) = (relative speed) × (time taken).

 

NOTE

 

• Opposite direction → relative speed = sum of speeds; same direction → relative speed = difference of speeds. This distinction is the most common source of error in such questions.

question: A shop that sells towels has offers going on, wherein customers can buy 2 towels and get 3 free. What is the percentage discount that the customer gets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 60%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Buy 2 towels and get 3 free, i.e. customer pays for 2 but takes home 5 towels.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Customer pays for 2 towels but receives 5 towels, so the effective 'free' portion = 5 − 2 = 3 towels out of 5.

 

• Discount % = (value not paid for ÷ total value) × 100 = (3/5) × 100 = 60%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In 'buy m get n free' offers, total items given = m + n, items paid for = m. Discount % = [(m + n − m)/(m + n)] × 100 = [n/(m+n)] × 100. Here n = 3, m+n = 5 ⇒ 3/5 = 60%.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is computing discount as (free items ÷ paid items) = 3/2 = 150%, which is wrong — discount % must always be taken on the total (marked) value, i.e. out of all 5 towels, not just the 2 paid for.

question: The ratio of the present ages of Shreya and her mother is 3 : 5 and the ratio of present ages of her mother and her grandmother is 10 : 13. If the average age of Shreya, her mother and her grandmother is 58 years, then find the present age of her mother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 60 years.

 

GIVEN

 

• Shreya : Mother = 3 : 5; Mother : Grandmother = 10 : 13; average age of all three = 58 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let mother's present age = M. Then Shreya's age = (3/5)M, and grandmother's age = (13/10)M (since mother : grandmother = 10 : 13).

 

• Sum of ages = 174 (since average of 3 people = 58 ⇒ total = 58 × 3 = 174).

 

• (3/5)M + M + (13/10)M = 174. Taking LCM = 10: (6/10)M + (10/10)M + (13/10)M = (29/10)M = 174.

 

• M = 174 × 10 ÷ 29 = 1740 ÷ 29 = 60 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Make all ratios share the common term (mother). Shreya : Mother : Grandmother = 3 : 5 : 5 × (13/10) = 6 : 10 : 13 (multiplying the first ratio by 2 to match mother = 10). Sum of parts = 6+10+13=29 parts = 174 ⇒ 1 part = 6; mother's age (10 parts) = 60.

 

NOTE

 

• When combining two ratios sharing a common person, first make the common term's value equal in both ratios before adding.

question: If third proportional of 9 and 60 be x, then what is the value of x?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 400.

 

GIVEN

 

• Third proportional of 9 and 60 is x, i.e. 9 : 60 :: 60 : x.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For third proportional: 9 : 60 = 60 : x ⇒ 9 × x = 60 × 60.

 

• x = 3600 ÷ 9 = 400.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Third proportional of a and b is always b²/a. Here, x = 60²/9 = 3600/9 = 400.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse 'third proportional' (b²/a) with 'mean proportional' (√(ab)) — they are different concepts frequently mixed up in exams.

question: Simplify: (4/7)² − 1/7 + 1/3.5 + 5(2/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 5 37/49.

 

GIVEN

 

• (4/7)² − 1/7 + 1/3.5 + 5(2/7)

 

SOLUTION

 

• (4/7)² = 16/49.

 

• 1/3.5 = 1/(7/2) = 2/7.

 

• 5(2/7) is the mixed number 5 + 2/7 = 37/7.

 

• Expression = 16/49 − 1/7 + 2/7 + 37/7 = 16/49 + (−1 + 2 + 37)/7 = 16/49 + 38/7.

 

• Convert 38/7 to a denominator of 49: 38/7 = 266/49.

 

• Sum = 16/49 + 266/49 = 282/49 = 5 remainder 37 (since 5×49 = 245, 282 − 245 = 37) = 5 37/49.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every term to a common denominator (49, the LCM of 49 and 7) right at the start, then add numerators in one shot instead of combining terms sequentially — this reduces the risk of arithmetic slips.

 

NOTE

 

• 1/3.5 is easily mis-simplified; always convert the decimal to a fraction first (3.5 = 7/2, so 1/3.5 = 2/7) before combining with other sevenths.

question: The diameter of a hemispherical bowl is 11.2 cm. How many litres of liquid can it hold? (Use π = 22/7 and round off your answer to three decimal places)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 0.368 litres.

 

GIVEN

 

• Diameter of hemispherical bowl = 11.2 cm ⇒ radius, r = 5.6 cm; π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3)πr³.

 

• r³ = 5.6³ = 5.6 × 5.6 × 5.6 = 31.36 × 5.6 = 175.616 cm³.

 

• Volume = (2/3) × (22/7) × 175.616 = (44/21) × 175.616 = 7727.104 ÷ 21 ≈ 367.957 cm³.

 

• Convert cm³ to litres (1 litre = 1000 cm³): 367.957 ÷ 1000 ≈ 0.368 litres.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a hemisphere, Volume = (2/3)πr³; always compute r³ carefully in stages (r² first, then × r) to avoid multiplication errors with decimals.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't forget the final unit conversion — the question asks for the answer in litres, not cm³ (1 litre = 1000 cm³), which is a common place marks are lost.

question: Two trains, 133 m and 227 m long, are moving in the same direction at speeds of 93 km/hr and 51 km/hr, respectively. How much time will the faster train take to completely cross the slower one?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 30 6/7 seconds.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train lengths: 133 m and 227 m; speeds: 93 km/hr and 51 km/hr, moving in the same direction.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Relative speed (same direction ⇒ speeds subtract) = 93 − 51 = 42 km/hr = 42 × 5/18 = 210/18 = 35/3 m/s.

 

• To completely cross each other, total distance covered = sum of the two lengths = 133 + 227 = 360 m.

 

• Time = distance ÷ relative speed = 360 ÷ (35/3) = 360 × 3/35 = 1080/35 = 216/7 = 30 6/7 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Completely cross' for two moving trains always means (sum of lengths) ÷ (relative speed), regardless of same or opposite direction — only the way relative speed is computed (sum vs. difference) changes.

 

NOTE

 

• Same direction → relative speed = difference of speeds; opposite direction → relative speed = sum of speeds.

question: The amount on a sum of ₹2,500 at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹3,025.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal, P = ₹2,500; Rate, R = 10% per annum, compounded annually; Time, T = 2 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Amount = P(1 + R/100)^T = 2500 × (1 + 10/100)² = 2500 × (1.1)².

 

• (1.1)² = 1.21.

 

• Amount = 2500 × 1.21 = ₹3,025.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 2 years at r% compound interest, Amount = P × (100 + r)²/100². Here Amount = 2500 × 110 × 110 ÷ 10000 = 2500 × 12100/10000 = 3025.

 

NOTE

 

• For 2 years, CI can also be found using CI = P[2r/100 + (r/100)²] = P × r(200 + r)/10000, then add to P for the amount: here CI = 2500 × 10 × 210/10000 = 525, Amount = 2500+525 = 3025.

question: In 330 litres solution of acid and water, the ratio of acid and water is 1:2. How many litres of acid must be added to it to get the solution in which the ratio of acid and water is 8:5?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 242.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total mixture = 330 L; acid : water = 1 : 2 (initially). Required final ratio, acid : water = 8 : 5.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Initial acid = (1/3) × 330 = 110 L; initial water = (2/3) × 330 = 220 L (water quantity stays fixed, since only acid is added).

 

• Let x litres of acid be added. New acid = 110 + x; water remains 220.

 

• New ratio: (110 + x)/220 = 8/5.

 

• Cross-multiply: 5(110 + x) = 8 × 220 ⇒ 550 + 5x = 1760 ⇒ 5x = 1210 ⇒ x = 242.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since only acid is added, water quantity (220 L) is the constant anchor. In the target ratio 8:5, water's part (5) corresponds to 220 L, so 1 part = 44 L; acid's part (8) = 352 L. Acid to be added = 352 − 110 = 242 L.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever only one component is added/removed, keep the other (unchanged) component's actual quantity fixed and scale the ratio around it — this is faster than forming and solving an equation from scratch.

question: A trader sells a watch at a loss of 28%. If he had sold it for ₹280 more, he would have made neither a profit nor a loss. What is the cost price of the watch?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹1,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Loss = 28%; selling ₹280 more would give no profit, no loss (i.e., SP would equal CP).

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Neither profit nor loss' means SP = CP if ₹280 more had been received.

 

• Current SP = CP − 28% of CP = 0.72 × CP (since a 28% loss means SP is 72% of CP).

 

• Given: CP − SP = ₹280 (the shortfall that would have made it break-even) ⇒ CP − 0.72 CP = 280 ⇒ 0.28 CP = 280.

 

• CP = 280 ÷ 0.28 = ₹1,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The gap between the actual loss-making SP and the break-even SP always equals (loss % of CP). So Loss% × CP = ₹280 (the extra amount) ⇒ 28% of CP = 280 ⇒ CP = 280 × 100/28 = ₹1,000.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Sold for ₹X more to make neither profit nor loss' always means: (that extra amount) = the original loss amount in rupees, since making up the loss exactly reaches CP.

question: The average age of 44 students of a class is 34 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 35 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 79.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 44 students = 34 years; including the teacher (45 people), average becomes 35 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total age of 44 students = 44 × 34 = 1496 years.

 

• Total age of 45 people (students + teacher) = 45 × 35 = 1575 years.

 

• Teacher's age = 1575 − 1496 = 79 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = (new average) + (number of students) × (increase in average) = 35 + 44 × (35 − 34) = 35 + 44 = 79.

 

NOTE

 

• When one new member raises the average of n existing members by d, that member's value = new average + n×d (since the new member must not only match the new average but also compensate for raising everyone else's shortfall).

question: If 4x/(0.75² − 0.25²) = 0.5, find the value of x.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 0.0625.

 

GIVEN

 

• 4x/(0.75² − 0.25²) = 0.5

 

SOLUTION

 

• 0.75² = 0.5625; 0.25² = 0.0625.

 

• Denominator = 0.5625 − 0.0625 = 0.5.

 

• Equation becomes: 4x/0.5 = 0.5.

 

• 4x = 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25.

 

• x = 0.25 ÷ 4 = 0.0625.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognise 0.75² − 0.25² as a difference of squares: (0.75 − 0.25)(0.75 + 0.25) = 0.5 × 1 = 0.5 — quicker than squaring each term separately.

 

NOTE

 

• a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is a valuable shortcut whenever you see two squared decimal/fraction terms subtracted.

question: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7. Find the sum of the numbers, if their HCF is 23.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 276.

 

GIVEN

 

• Two numbers are in ratio 5 : 7; their HCF = 23.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since the ratio 5 : 7 is already in lowest terms (5 and 7 are co-prime), the actual numbers are 5 × 23 and 7 × 23.

 

• Numbers = 115 and 161.

 

• Sum = 115 + 161 = 276.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two numbers are in ratio a : b (a, b co-prime) with HCF = h, the numbers are simply ah and bh, and their sum is h(a + b). Here: 23 × (5 + 7) = 23 × 12 = 276.

 

NOTE

 

• The HCF of two numbers in ratio a : b (in lowest terms) is always the common multiplying factor, since a and b share no common factor themselves.

question: One pipe can fill a tank in 10 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 20 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 10.

 

GIVEN

 

• Filling pipe: fills the tank in 10 minutes; emptying pipe: empties a full tank in 20 minutes; both opened together starting from empty.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Filling pipe's rate = 1/10 tank/min; emptying pipe's rate = −1/20 tank/min.

 

• Combined rate = 1/10 − 1/20 = 2/20 − 1/20 = 1/20 tank/min.

 

• Time to fill the full tank at this combined rate = 1 ÷ (1/20) = 20 minutes.

 

• Time to fill half the tank = 20/2 = 10 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combined rate with an emptying pipe = (1/fill time) − (1/empty time). Since the combined process is uniform (constant net rate), time for half tank is simply half of the time for the full tank.

 

NOTE

 

• Always subtract the emptying pipe's rate (never add it) when it works against the filling pipe.

question: In a triangle with sides 12 units, 5 units and 13 units, the perpendiculars are drawn from all vertices. The length of the smallest perpendicular (in units) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 60/13 units.

 

GIVEN

 

• Triangle with sides 12, 5, 13 units.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13² — this is a right-angled triangle, right angle between the sides 5 and 12.

 

• Area = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 sq units.

 

• Altitude (perpendicular) to any side = 2 × Area ÷ (that side).

 

• Altitude to side 13 (hypotenuse) = 2 × 30 ÷ 13 = 60/13 ≈ 4.62.

 

• Altitude to side 12 = 2 × 30 ÷ 12 = 5.

 

• Altitude to side 5 = 2 × 30 ÷ 5 = 12.

 

• Comparing 60/13 (≈4.62), 5, and 12 — the smallest is 60/13.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The perpendicular is smallest when drawn to the largest side, since altitude = 2×Area/side is inversely proportional to the side length. So directly compute the altitude to the hypotenuse (largest side, 13) to get the smallest altitude.

 

NOTE

 

• 5-12-13 is a Pythagorean triplet — recognise it instantly to skip verifying the right angle from scratch.

question: The marks of P are 10 more than the marks of Q. The marks of Q are 10 more than half of the marks of P. The marks of Q are ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 30.

 

GIVEN

 

• P = Q + 10; Q = (P/2) + 10.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute P = Q + 10 into the second equation: Q = (Q + 10)/2 + 10.

 

• Multiply through by 2: 2Q = (Q + 10) + 20 = Q + 30.

 

• 2Q − Q = 30 ⇒ Q = 30.

 

• (Check: P = Q + 10 = 40; half of P = 20, plus 10 = 30 = Q. ✓)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up both relations as simple linear equations in one variable and substitute immediately — with only two unknowns and two relations, this is faster than trial-and-error with the options.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify your final answer by substituting back into both original conditions, as done above, to catch sign or substitution errors.

question: A man standing on the line joining the feet of two towers of heights 10 m, 15 m observes the top of the towers with the angles of elevation 45° and 60°, respectively. What is the distance (in metres) between the feet of two towers (take √3 = 1.73)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 18.65 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Tower 1 height = 10 m, angle of elevation = 45°; Tower 2 height = 15 m, angle of elevation = 60°; man stands between the two towers on the line joining their feet; √3 = 1.73.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let d1 = horizontal distance from the man to tower 1 (height 10 m). tan 45° = 10/d1 ⇒ 1 = 10/d1 ⇒ d1 = 10 m.

 

• Let d2 = horizontal distance from the man to tower 2 (height 15 m). tan 60° = 15/d2 ⇒ √3 = 15/d2 ⇒ d2 = 15/√3 = 15√3/3 = 5√3 = 5 × 1.73 = 8.65 m.

 

• Since the man stands between the two towers, distance between the feet of the towers = d1 + d2 = 10 + 8.65 = 18.65 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• tan 45° = 1 gives distance = height directly; tan 60° = √3 gives distance = height/√3 = height×√3/3. Compute both quickly and simply add them (since the man is between the towers).

 

NOTE

 

• Rationalise 15/√3 to 5√3 before substituting the value of √3, to avoid an extra division step.

question: In an election, four candidates received 1242, 832, 1426 and 1100 votes, respectively. The difference between the winning candidate's votes percentage and runner up candidate vote percentage is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 4%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Votes received by 4 candidates: 1242, 832, 1426, 1100.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total votes = 1242 + 832 + 1426 + 1100 = 4600.

 

• Winning candidate = 1426 votes (highest); runner-up = 1242 votes (next highest).

 

• Winner's % = (1426/4600) × 100 = 31.0%.

 

• Runner-up's % = (1242/4600) × 100 = 27.0%.

 

• Difference = 31.0% − 27.0% = 4%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Compute the vote difference first (1426 − 1242 = 184), then convert directly to a percentage of total: (184/4600) × 100 = 4% — this avoids finding two separate percentages.

 

NOTE

 

• Always identify the top two vote-getters correctly by ranking all four values before computing percentages — a wrong pick of 'runner-up' is a common error.

question: If the radius of a sphere is decreased by 25% and becomes 6 cm, find the decrease in its volume.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 394 2/3 π cm³.

 

GIVEN

 

• Radius decreased by 25% becomes 6 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let original radius = R. After a 25% decrease, new radius = 0.75R = 6 ⇒ R = 6/0.75 = 8 cm.

 

• Original volume = (4/3)πR³ = (4/3)π(8)³ = (4/3)π(512) = 2048π/3.

 

• New volume = (4/3)π(6)³ = (4/3)π(216) = 864π/3.

 

• Decrease in volume = 2048π/3 − 864π/3 = 1184π/3 = 394 (2/3) π cm³ (since 1184 ÷ 3 = 394 remainder 2).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Volume ∝ r³. Find original radius first (here R = 6/0.75 = 8), then compute decrease = (4/3)π(R³ − r³) directly in one step rather than finding both volumes and subtracting separately.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Decreased by 25% and becomes 6' means 6 is 75% of the original — always translate 'becomes' word problems into (new value) = (1 − %decrease) × (original), and solve for the original first.

question: A person saves 60% of his income. If his expenditure is ₹520, then his income (in ₹) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1300.

 

GIVEN

 

• Savings = 60% of income; expenditure = ₹520.

 

SOLUTION

 

• If savings = 60% of income, expenditure = 100% − 60% = 40% of income.

 

• 40% of income = ₹520.

 

• Income = 520 ÷ 0.40 = ₹1,300.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Expenditure % = 100 − Savings % = 40%. Income = Expenditure × (100/Expenditure%) = 520 × (100/40) = 520 × 2.5 = 1300.

 

NOTE

 

• Income = Savings + Expenditure always; the two percentages (savings % and expenditure %) must together add up to 100%.

question: If x^(2m) × y⁵ × x²/y^(m−1) = (y²x³)², find the value of m.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• x^(2m) × y⁵ × x² / y^(m−1) = (y²x³)²

 

SOLUTION

 

• Simplify the RHS: (y²x³)² = y⁴x⁶.

 

• Simplify the LHS exponents: for x, 2m + 2; for y, 5 − (m − 1) = 6 − m.

 

• So LHS = x^(2m+2) × y^(6−m).

 

• Equate powers of x: 2m + 2 = 6 ⇒ 2m = 4 ⇒ m = 2.

 

• Equate powers of y (check): 6 − m = 4 ⇒ m = 2. Both give the same value, confirming consistency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since a product of powers of the SAME base has exponents that simply add/subtract, collect x's and y's exponents separately and equate each side's powers — no need to expand anything numerically.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check using BOTH variables' exponent equations — if they don't give the same value of the unknown, there's an arithmetic error somewhere.

question: A child inflates a balloon, increasing its size by 50%. Later, while tying it, the balloon's size decreases by 20%. What is the overall percentage change in the size of the balloon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 20% (increment).

 

GIVEN

 

• First a 50% increase, then a 20% decrease, applied successively.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Multiply the successive factors: (1 + 50/100) × (1 − 20/100) = 1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2.

 

• A final factor of 1.2 means a net 20% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Net % change for successive % changes a% and b% = a + b + (ab/100). Here: 50 + (−20) + (50 × −20)/100 = 30 − 10 = 20% increase.

 

NOTE

 

• Successive percentage changes must always be multiplied as factors, never simply added — a common mistake here would be to say 50% − 20% = 30%, which is incorrect.

question: The average of the first 7 odd natural numbers is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• First 7 odd natural numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 13 = 49.

 

• Average = Sum ÷ Count = 49 ÷ 7 = 7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The average of the first n odd natural numbers is always exactly n (since they form an AP with first term 1 and common difference 2, whose mean equals the middle term). Here n = 7, so the average is directly 7 — no need to add all terms.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't confuse this with the average of the first n natural numbers, which is (n+1)/2, or the first n even numbers, whose average is (n+1).

question: Each of the digits in the number 7123458 is arranged in ascending order from left to right. What will be the sum of the digits which are second from the left and second from the right in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 9.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 7123458. Digits are to be arranged in ascending order.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Digits of 7123458: 7, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8.

 

• Arranged in ascending order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8.

 

• Second digit from the left = 2.

 

• Second digit from the right = 7 (rightmost is 8, second from right is 7).

 

• Sum = 2 + 7 = 9.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Just sort the digits once; 'second from left' is simply the 2nd digit of the sorted list, and 'second from right' is the (n−1)th digit — no need to redo the sort for each part.

 

NOTE

 

• Sort the digits carefully and double count from each end — miscounting the position is the most common slip in such questions.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete?

LNT 81, PKP 75, THL 69, XEH 63, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. BBD 57.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: LNT 81, PKP 75, THL 69, XEH 63, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Numbers: 81, 75, 69, 63 decrease by 6 each time ⇒ next = 63 − 6 = 57.

 

• 1st letters: L(12), P(16), T(20), X(24) — increase by 4 each time ⇒ next = 24 + 4 = 28 → 28 − 26 = 2 = B.

 

• 2nd letters: N(14), K(11), H(8), E(5) — decrease by 3 each time ⇒ next = 5 − 3 = 2 = B.

 

• 3rd letters: T(20), P(16), L(12), H(8) — decrease by 4 each time ⇒ next = 8 − 4 = 4 = D.

 

• Combining: BBD 57.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a letter-number cluster series into separate columns (1st letters, 2nd letters, 3rd letters, numbers) and find the arithmetic pattern in each column independently — much faster than trying to see one combined pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• When a letter position 'wraps around' past Z (26), subtract 26 to get back into the A–Z range (here 28 → 28−26 = 2 = B).

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order?

EWR ASN WOJ SKF ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. OGB.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: EWR, ASN, WOJ, SKF, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: E(5), A(1), W(23), S(19) — each term decreases by 4 (with wraparound: 5−4=1; 1−4=−3→23; 23−4=19; 19−4=15) ⇒ next = 15 = O.

 

• 2nd letters: W(23), S(19), O(15), K(11) — each decreases by 4 ⇒ next = 11−4=7 = G.

 

• 3rd letters: R(18), N(14), J(10), F(6) — each decreases by 4 ⇒ next = 6−4=2 = B.

 

• Combining: OGB.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Notice all three columns share the same step (−4); once you spot that in one column, quickly verify it in the others rather than solving each from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• For 'decreasing past A', wrap around using: if the result is ≤ 0, add 26 to bring it back into range (e.g., 1−4=−3 → −3+26=23=W).

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All apples are fruits.

Some fruits are sweet.

Conclusions:

(I) Some apples are sweet.

(II) All sweet are apples.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: All apples are fruits (A → F, a universal affirmative).

 

• Statement 2: Some fruits are sweet (F ∩ Sweet ≠ ∅, a particular affirmative).

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'All apples are fruits' means the apple set is fully inside the fruit set.

 

• 'Some fruits are sweet' only tells us that a portion of fruits overlaps with 'sweet' — but there is no guarantee that this sweet portion overlaps with the apple portion of the fruit set. The 'sweet' fruits could be entirely non-apple fruits (like mangoes).

 

• Conclusion I ('Some apples are sweet'): does NOT necessarily follow, since the given information does not confirm any overlap between apples specifically and the sweet fruits.

 

• Conclusion II ('All sweet are apples'): does NOT follow either — this reverses and over-generalises a particular statement into a universal one, which is never valid in syllogisms.

 

• Since neither conclusion is guaranteed to be true in every possible case consistent with the statements, neither follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a simple Venn diagram: draw the Fruit circle with the Apple circle fully inside it, then shade 'sweet' as a separate overlapping portion of Fruit that does NOT have to touch Apple. If you can draw even one valid diagram where a conclusion is false, that conclusion does not follow.

 

NOTE

 

• A common trap: 'All A are B, Some B are C' NEVER validly gives 'Some A are C' — this is a classic syllogism fallacy to watch for in reasoning sections.

question: A, B, C, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. R is the immediate neighbour of both C and T. T sits third to the left of U. B sits to the immediate left of U. S is not an immediate neighbour of T. Who sits second to the right of A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. U.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A, B, C, R, S, T, U) sit around a circular table facing the centre. R is adjacent to both C and T (so T-R-C are three consecutive seats). T is third to the left of U. B is immediate left of U. S is not adjacent to T.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take U as a fixed reference point. Moving in the 'left' direction from U: B is immediate left of U (1 seat away); T is third to the left of U (3 seats away).

 

• Since R is adjacent to BOTH C and T, the three must sit consecutively as T-R-C (R sits directly between T and C).

 

• Placing T-R-C consecutively next to T (on the side away from U/B) fixes R and C's seats.

 

• The only two seats now left are for A and S. Since S cannot be an immediate neighbour of T, and one of the two remaining seats IS adjacent to T, S must take the other (non-adjacent) seat, leaving A in the seat adjacent to T.

 

• With everyone's seat fixed, counting two seats to the right of A (in the circular order) lands exactly on U.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular seating with 'facing the centre', always fix one clearly defined person (here U) first, place directional clues (left/right of a reference) around them, then resolve any 'X is neighbour of both Y and Z' clue as three people sitting consecutively — this eliminates most of the guesswork.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Facing the centre': a person's left hand points in the clockwise direction (as normally drawn) and their right hand points counter-clockwise — get this convention fixed before placing anyone, and use it consistently throughout.

question: Rajesh ranked 38th from the top and 27th from the bottom in his class. How many students are there in his class?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 64.

 

GIVEN

 

• Rajesh's rank from the top = 38th; rank from the bottom = 27th.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total students = (rank from top) + (rank from bottom) − 1 (Rajesh is counted once in both ranks, so 1 is subtracted).

 

• Total = 38 + 27 − 1 = 64.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always remember the formula: Total = (Rank from top) + (Rank from bottom) − 1, applicable whenever one person's two ranks (from either end) are given.

 

NOTE

 

• Forgetting to subtract 1 (double-counting Rajesh) is the most common mistake in this type of question.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(Note: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(15, 28, 64)

(63, 76, 112)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. (74, 87, 123).

 

GIVEN

 

• Reference sets: (15, 28, 64) and (63, 76, 112), both following the same underlying pattern.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In (15, 28, 64): 28 − 15 = 13; 64 − 28 = 36.

 

• In (63, 76, 112): 76 − 63 = 13; 112 − 76 = 36.
