• Both reference sets follow the same relation: second number = first + 13; third number = second + 36.

 

• Check option A, (74, 87, 123): 87 − 74 = 13 ✓; 123 − 87 = 36 ✓ — pattern matches exactly.

 

• Check option B, (44, 57, 83): 57 − 44 = 13 ✓, but 83 − 57 = 26 ✗ — pattern fails.

 

• Check option C, (82, 95, 132): 95 − 82 = 13 ✓, but 132 − 95 = 37 ✗ — pattern fails.

 

• Check option D, (159, 172, 207): 172 − 159 = 13 ✓, but 207 − 172 = 35 ✗ — pattern fails.

 

• Only option A satisfies both differences (13 and 36).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two reference sets are given, first find the relation (here, constant differences) common to BOTH of them — that confirms the true pattern — then test each option against that exact same relation.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly disallows breaking numbers into digits; always look first at simple differences/ratios between the whole numbers in a set.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for '×', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

64 A 8 C 4 B 11 D 3 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 49.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −. Expression: 64 A 8 C 4 B 11 D 3 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the actual symbols: 64 ÷ 8 + 4 × 11 − 3.

 

• Apply BODMAS: division and multiplication first — 64 ÷ 8 = 8; 4 × 11 = 44.

 

• Now: 8 + 44 − 3 = 52 − 3 = 49.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First mentally substitute all coded letters with their actual symbols in one pass, then solve using standard BODMAS — don't try to compute while still reading letters, as that increases the chance of a substitution error.

 

NOTE

 

• Always perform division/multiplication before addition/subtraction (BODMAS), regardless of the left-to-right order in which the coded letters appear.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster pair that DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:

question: Each of the digits in the number 8312467 is arranged in ascending order from left to right. What will be the sum of the digits which are second from the left and second from the right in the new number thus formed?

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All roads are trucks.

No truck is a sheep.

Conclusions:

(I) Some roads are sheep.

(II) All trucks are sheep.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statement 1: All roads are trucks (Road ⊆ Truck).

 

• Statement 2: No truck is a sheep (Truck ∩ Sheep = ∅).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Since all roads are trucks, and no truck is a sheep, it logically follows that no road is a sheep either (roads being a subset of trucks, which have zero overlap with sheep).

 

• Conclusion I ('Some roads are sheep'): directly contradicts the valid deduction that no road is a sheep — so it does NOT follow.

 

• Conclusion II ('All trucks are sheep'): directly contradicts the given Statement 2 itself ('No truck is a sheep') — so it clearly does NOT follow.

 

• Since both conclusions are false given the statements, neither follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw a quick Venn diagram: draw Road fully inside Truck, and Truck completely separate from (not touching) Sheep. This visually confirms Road and Sheep also don't touch, instantly ruling out both conclusions.

 

NOTE

 

• 'All A are B' + 'No B is C' always validly gives 'No A is C' — memorise this standard syllogism combination, as it appears frequently.

question:
Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row, facing north.

Only three people sit to the right of C. Only four people sit between A and B, neither of whom sits on the left end. D sits immediately to the left of F. Only three people sit between G and B. How many people sit between F and G?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A–G) in a row (positions 1 to 7, left to right). Only 3 sit to the right of C. Only 4 sit between A and B (neither at the left end). D is immediately left of F. Only 3 sit between G and B.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only three sit to the right of C' ⇒ C is at position 4 (positions 5, 6, 7 are to its right).

 

• 'Only 4 sit between A and B' ⇒ their positions differ by 5. Possible pairs: (1,6) or (2,7). Since neither A nor B is at the left end (position 1), the pair (1,6) is rejected ⇒ A and B occupy positions 2 and 7 (in some order).

 

• Testing B = 7: 'Only 3 sit between G and B' ⇒ G is at position 7−4 = 3. Then A = 2.

 

• Remaining positions 1, 5, 6 are for D, E, F. Since D is immediately left of F, they must be consecutive — only (5,6) works ⇒ D = 5, F = 6, leaving E = 1.

 

• (Testing B = 2 instead leads to no valid consecutive placement for D-F among the remaining positions, so it is rejected.)

 

• Final arrangement: 1-E, 2-A, 3-G, 4-C, 5-D, 6-F, 7-B.

 

• Between F (position 6) and G (position 3): positions 4 and 5 (C and D) — 2 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every 'only N sit to the right/between' clue into a direct position number immediately (using position = total − N for 'right of' clues), and test the two branches of any 'either/or' clue (like A/B = 2,7) quickly — the branch that fails a later constraint (like D-F being consecutive) is automatically eliminated.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Neither of whom sits on the left end' is a critical filter clue — always apply such exclusions immediately to narrow down the possible position pairs before proceeding.

question:
O, P, Q, R, W, X, and Y are sitting in a straight line facing the north. No one sits to the left of P. Only four people sit between P and Q. Only three people sit to the right of Y. X sits to the immediate left of R. W is not an immediate neighbour of Y.

Who sits third to the left of W?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Y.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (O, P, Q, R, W, X, Y) in a row, positions 1–7. No one is to the left of P. 4 sit between P and Q. 3 sit to the right of Y. X is immediately left of R. W is not adjacent to Y.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'No one to the left of P' ⇒ P is at position 1.

 

• 'Only 4 sit between P and Q' ⇒ their positions differ by 5 ⇒ Q is at position 1+5 = 6.

 

• 'Only 3 sit to the right of Y' ⇒ Y is at position 7−3 = 4.

 

• Remaining positions: 2, 3, 5, 7 for O, W, X, R. Since X is immediately left of R, they must be consecutive — only (2,3) fits among the remaining positions ⇒ X = 2, R = 3.

 

• Remaining positions 5 and 7 are for O and W. Since W cannot be adjacent to Y (position 4), and position 5 IS adjacent to Y, W cannot be at 5 ⇒ W = 7, O = 5.

 

• Final arrangement: 1-P, 2-X, 3-R, 4-Y, 5-O, 6-Q, 7-W.

 

• Third to the left of W (position 7): 7 − 3 = position 4 = Y.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert 'no one to the left of X' clues to position 1 immediately, and 'only N to the right' clues to position (total − N) immediately — this fixes several people before you even need to consider the trickier relative clues.

 

NOTE

 

• After placing the fixed-position people, always check which of the remaining slots are 'adjacent' to a named person before assigning the last few people — this is exactly how W's position was resolved here.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means 'A is the mother of B',

A – B means 'A is the father of B',

A * B means 'A is the husband of B', and

A ÷ B means 'A is the sister of B'.

Based on the above, how is P related to T if 'P – Q ÷ R * S + T'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Father's Father.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: '+' = mother of; '−' = father of; '*' = husband of; '÷' = sister of. Expression: P − Q ÷ R * S + T.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Read the expression as a chain of relations, left to right: P − Q: P is the father of Q.

 

• Q ÷ R: Q is the sister of R ⇒ Q and R are siblings, so they share the same father — meaning P is also R's father.

 

• **R * S**: R is the husband of S ⇒ R and S are a married couple.

 

• S + T: S is the mother of T ⇒ since S is R's wife and T's mother, R is T's father.

 

• So T's father is R, and R's father is P ⇒ P is T's paternal grandfather, i.e. Father's Father.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In such blood-relation coded-symbol questions, build a small family tree step by step from left to right using the decoded relation at each symbol — trying to solve it all mentally without a sketch often leads to errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Whenever two people are linked as siblings ('sister of'), remember they automatically share the SAME parents — this is often the key link connecting two otherwise separate parts of the relation chain.

question:
Refer to the number and symbol series given below and answer the question that follows. Counting to be done from left to right only. (All numbers are single-digit numbers only.)

(Left) 3 @ 2 ^ @ % \ 8 9 \ / ? 8 7 6 # & # + 7 \ (Right)

How many such symbols are there each of which is immediately preceded by a number and also immediately followed by a number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series (left to right): 3, @, 2, ^, @, %, \, 8, 9, \, /, ?, 8, 7, 6, #, &, #, +, 7, \

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check every non-number symbol to see if it has a number immediately before AND immediately after it:

 

• @ (position 2): preceded by 3 (number) ✓, followed by 2 (number) ✓ — qualifies.

 

• ^: preceded by 2 (number) ✓, but followed by @ (symbol) ✗ — fails.

 

• @ (2nd occurrence), %, \, /, ?: each is either preceded or followed by another symbol rather than a number — fails.

 

• \ (after 9): preceded by 9 (number) ✓, but followed by / (symbol) ✗ — fails.

 

• #, &, #, +: each is sandwiched between other symbols on at least one side — fails, except the first '#' which is preceded by 6 (number) but followed by & (symbol) — fails.

 

• \ (final, at the end): preceded by 7 (number) ✓, but has no symbol/number after it (it's the last term) — fails.

 

• Only ONE symbol — the first @ — satisfies both conditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Go through the series once, marking each token as 'N' (number) or 'S' (symbol); then scan for the specific pattern N-S-N to instantly spot qualifying symbols, rather than re-checking each symbol's neighbours separately from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• The last and first terms of the series can never qualify for a 'preceded by...and followed by...' condition if they lack a neighbour on one side — always exclude the two end terms from consideration for such counts unless the series wraps around (which it does not here).

question:

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. SX-UR.

SOLUTION

question: Town U is to the north of Town V. Town W is to the east of Town U. Town X is to the south of Town W. Town Y is to the west of Town X. Town V is to the south-west of Town Y. What is the position of Town U with respect to Town Y?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. North-west.

 

GIVEN

 

• U is north of V. W is east of U. X is south of W. Y is west of X. V is south-west of Y.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Set up a direction diagram: starting from U, go south to reach V; go east from U to reach W; go south from W to reach X; go west from X to reach Y.

 

• Plotting these moves on a grid (taking U as a convenient reference point) places: V is south of U; W is east of U; X is south-east of U (east then south); Y is south-east of U as well, but less far east than X (since Y is west of X) and further south than U's row.

 

• The condition 'V is south-west of Y' confirms Y lies further east and further north than V, which is consistent with Y sitting to the south-east of U overall.

 

• Reading the diagram, U — relative to Y — lies to the north-west: U is both north of Y (Y took a southward path via W then X) and west of Y (Y is east of the U-V line).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For multi-step direction puzzles, plot each town's position as coordinates on a simple (x, y) grid one clue at a time (with consistent unit steps: north = +y, east = +x), and simply read off the relative direction using the sign of the difference in coordinates at the end.

 

NOTE

 

• Direction questions are best solved by drawing, even roughly — attempting to track five separate directional clues purely mentally is a common source of error.

question: Seven boxes A, B, C, D, I, J and K are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. Only B is kept above I. Only C is kept between I and J. Only A is kept below K. How many boxes are kept between D and A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes (A, B, C, D, I, J, K) stacked vertically. Only B is above I. Only C is between I and J. Only A is below K.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number the positions 1 (bottom) to 7 (top). 'Only B is above I' means exactly one box (B) is above I ⇒ I = position 6, B = position 7 (top).

 

• 'Only A is below K' means exactly one box (A) is below K ⇒ A = position 1 (bottom), K = position 2.

 

• 'Only C is between I and J' means exactly one box (C) lies between I(6) and J ⇒ J is 2 positions from I ⇒ J = position 4, with C = position 5 in between.

 

• The only remaining position, 3, is for D.

 

• Final stack (bottom to top): 1-A, 2-K, 3-D, 4-J, 5-C, 6-I, 7-B.

 

• Between D (position 3) and A (position 1): position 2 (K) lies in between — 1 box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Only X is above/below Y' clues directly fix TWO positions at once (Y near one end, X at the very end) — always resolve these extreme-position clues first before tackling the 'between' clues, which then narrow down based on the already-fixed positions.

question: MU 4 is related to PO −10 in a certain way. In the same way, DL 8 is related to GF −6. To which of the given options is HP 12 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. KJ −2.

 

GIVEN

 

• MU 4 → PO −10. DL 8 → GF −6. Find the pair related to HP 12 the same way.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Letters: M→P is +3 (13→16); U→O is −6 (21→15). Check with the second pair: D→G is +3 (4→7); L→F is −6 (12→6). Confirmed: 1st letter +3, 2nd letter −6.

 

• Numbers: from 4 to −10 is a change of −14; from 8 to −6 is also a change of −14. Confirmed: number changes by −14.

 

• Apply to HP 12: H(8) + 3 = 11 = K; P(16) − 6 = 10 = J ⇒ new letters = KJ.

 

• Number: 12 − 14 = −2.

 

• So HP 12 relates to KJ −2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In such 'coded pair' analogy questions with two given examples, find the fixed shift separately for each letter position and for the number using BOTH examples to confirm consistency, then apply the exact same three shifts to the new term.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify your discovered pattern against BOTH given example pairs (not just one) before applying it — a pattern that only fits one example may be a coincidence.

question:

• The next pair should be (base number, its square) where the square is 144.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

• Spot that every alternate term is a perfect square of the term just before it (8→64=8², 9→81=9², etc.); then simply take the square root of 144 to instantly get the missing term.

 

NOTE

 

• Memorising squares up to at least 20² (400) makes such number-series questions much faster to solve.

question:

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

question:

question: Himangi starts from Point A and drives 2 km towards the east. She then takes a right turn, drives 7 km, turns left and drives 9 km. She then takes a left turn and drives 3 km. She takes a final left turn, drives 11 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should she drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 4 km towards the north.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start at A. Move 2 km east; right turn, 7 km; left turn, 9 km; left turn, 3 km; left turn, 11 km, stop at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Track direction changes starting facing east: right turn from east → facing south; then left turn from south → facing east; then left turn from east → facing north; then left turn from north → facing west.

 

• Taking A = (0, 0), east = +x, north = +y:

 

• Move 1: 2 km east → (2, 0).

 

• Move 2: 7 km south → (2, −7).

 

• Move 3: 9 km east → (11, −7).

 

• Move 4: 3 km north → (11, −4).

 

• Move 5: 11 km west → (0, −4). This is Point P.

 

• To return to A (0, 0) from P (0, −4): same x-coordinate, so only need to move in the y-direction — 4 km north.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the net east-west and net north-south displacement (sum positive/negative movements in each axis separately) rather than plotting every intermediate point — the final direction back to start is simply the reverse of the net (x, y) displacement.

 

NOTE

 

• Carefully update the facing direction after EVERY turn (right turn = 90° clockwise, left turn = 90° counter-clockwise) — a single missed turn changes all subsequent directions.

question: Which of the following ministries launched the State Health Regulatory Excellence Index (SHRESTH), a first-of-its-kind national initiative to benchmark and strengthen state drug regulatory systems through a transparent, data-driven framework in August 2025?

question: Which organ under MHA launched the e‑Zero FIR system for cyber‑fraud cases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The e-Zero FIR system, aimed at speeding up the registration of FIRs for high-value cyber-fraud cases, was launched by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), which functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). (I4C — साइबर अपराध समन्वय केंद्र)

 

• Under this system, cyber-fraud complaints (typically above a threshold monetary value) reported on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or the 1930 helpline are auto-converted into a Zero FIR, enabling faster police action without jurisdictional delays.

 

• A Zero FIR can be registered at any police station regardless of the jurisdiction in which the crime occurred, and is later transferred to the police station with actual jurisdiction — this rapid registration is critical for freezing fraudulent transactions quickly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• I4C was set up in 2020 to act as the nodal agency to deal with cybercrime in India in a coordinated and comprehensive manner, working closely with states/UTs and central agencies.

 

• I4C also runs the 1930 Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting helpline and the CyTrain platform for training police personnel in cybercrime investigation.

 

• Other I4C initiatives include the Suspect Registry, Samanvaya platform, and the Chakshu facility for reporting suspected fraud communications.

 

NOTE

 

• Cyber Appellate Tribunal (Option A): A tribunal (once) meant to hear appeals under the IT Act; not the body that launched e-Zero FIR.

 

• State Police of India (Option B): State police forces implement FIR registration on the ground, but the e-Zero FIR system itself was launched at the national level by I4C.

 

• Central Bureau of Investigation (Option D): India's premier investigation agency, but not the body responsible for launching the e-Zero FIR cyber-fraud initiative.

question: Which lake, known as India's longest and a Ramsar site in Kerala is currently facing severe ecological degradation?

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chilika Lake (Odisha) is Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon and India's largest coastal lagoon, also a Ramsar site, famous for migratory birds and Irrawaddy dolphins.

 

• Loktak Lake (Manipur) is the largest freshwater lake in North-East India, famous for its floating islands (phumdis) and the Keibul Lamjao National Park.

 

• India has over 75 Ramsar sites as of 2025, the highest number in South Asia.

 

NOTE

 

• Loktak Lake (Option B): The largest freshwater lake in North-East India, not India's longest lake, and located in Manipur, not Kerala.

 

• Chilika Lake (Option C): India's largest lagoon, located in Odisha, not Kerala.

 

• Pulicat Lake (Option D): India's second-largest brackish-water lagoon, located between Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, not Kerala.

• Vadodara (Option A), Surat (Option C) and Rajkot (Option D): All major cities in Gujarat, but the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex inaugurated in September 2025 is located in Ahmedabad, not these cities.

question: In 2025, which of the following states emerged as the national leader in mangrove afforestation, covering 19020 hectares in just two years under the Centre's 'MISHTI' scheme, launched in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gujarat emerged as the national leader in mangrove afforestation under the MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) scheme, achieving coverage of 19,020 hectares within just two years of the scheme's launch. (गुजरात — मैंग्रोव रोपण में देश में अग्रणी, मिष्टी योजना)

 

• MISHTI was launched by the Government of India in the Union Budget 2023-24, aimed at intensive afforestation of mangroves along the coastline and salt-pan lands, combining efforts under MGNREGS, CAMPA (Compensatory Afforestation Fund), and other funding sources.

 

• Gujarat's long coastline (India's longest, among states) and existing mangrove ecosystems (like in the Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat) gave it a natural advantage in scaling up this initiative rapidly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees/shrubs that grow in coastal intertidal zones, providing critical ecosystem services like coastal protection from storms/erosion, carbon sequestration ('blue carbon'), and breeding grounds for marine life.

 

• Other major mangrove regions in India include the Sundarbans (West Bengal) — the largest mangrove forest in India — and the mangroves of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

 

• CAMPA (Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority) manages funds collected from industries for diverting forest land, used for afforestation projects like MISHTI.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option A), Maharashtra (Option B) and Uttar Pradesh (Option C): All have their own environmental initiatives, but the national leadership position in MISHTI mangrove afforestation in 2025 was held by Gujarat.

question: In which sport did Indian athletes secure a mixed relay medal at the 2025 Asian Indoor Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mixed relay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian athletes secured a medal in the mixed relay event at the 2025 Asian Indoor Games, reflecting India's growing depth in athletics events involving both male and female team members competing together. (मिश्रित रिले — 2025 एशियन इंडोर गेम्स)

 

• Mixed relay events (such as the mixed 4x400m relay) are a relatively newer addition to major athletics competitions, requiring teams to field a combination of male and female athletes.

 

• The Asian Indoor Games, organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA), features indoor versions of various sports, providing athletes a platform outside the traditional outdoor Asian Games calendar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has also achieved notable success in the mixed 4x400m relay at global stages, including a bronze medal at the World Athletics Championships.

 

• The Asian Games (outdoor, quadrennial) is the larger, more prominent multi-sport event in Asia, distinct from the Asian Indoor Games, both organised under the OCA umbrella.

 

• India's athletics programme has been strengthened through schemes like the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and Khelo India.

 

NOTE

 

• Shooting (Option A), Swimming (Option B) and Wrestling (Option C): All sports where India has a strong presence at multi-sport games, but the specific mixed relay medal referenced in this question was in athletics (mixed relay), not these disciplines.

question: As per the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the target for nuclear power capacity of India by 2047?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 100GW.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Union Budget 2025-26, the Government of India set a target of 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047, marking the centenary of India's independence, under the newly announced Nuclear Energy Mission. (नाभिकीय ऊर्जा मिशन — 2047 तक 100 गीगावाट लक्ष्य)

 

• The Nuclear Energy Mission for Viksit Bharat was announced in the Budget 2025-26, along with plans to amend the Atomic Energy Act and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act to enable greater private sector participation in the nuclear power sector.

 

• The Budget also announced an outlay of ₹20,000 crore for the research and development of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), targeting operationalisation of at least 5 indigenously developed SMRs by 2033.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's current installed nuclear power capacity (as of the mid-2020s) is around 8 GW, operated primarily by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).

 

• Major Indian nuclear power plants include Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu), Tarapur (Maharashtra), Kakrapar (Gujarat), and Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu).

 

• India's nuclear programme has historically followed a three-stage strategy, envisioned by Dr. Homi J. Bhabha, aimed at eventually utilising India's abundant thorium reserves.

 

NOTE

 

• 150GW (Option A), 50GW (Option C) and 80GW (Option D): These figures do not match the officially announced target of 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047.

question: Who among the following was elected as the 80th president of United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in June 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annalena Baerbock.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annalena Baerbock, the former German Foreign Minister, was elected as the President of the 80th session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in June 2025. (एनालेना बेयरबॉक — 80वें संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा अध्यक्ष)

 

• The UNGA President serves a one-year term, presiding over the General Assembly's plenary sessions, and the position rotates annually among the UN's five regional groups.

 

• Baerbock's election reflects continued German engagement in multilateral diplomacy following her tenure as Germany's top diplomat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The United Nations General Assembly, headquartered in New York, is the main deliberative organ of the UN, comprising all 193 member states, each with one vote.

 

• The UN Secretary-General (as of the mid-2020s) is António Guterres of Portugal, a separate and distinct role from the rotating UNGA President.

 

• India has previously held the UNGA presidency through figures like Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit (1953), the first woman to hold the position.

 

NOTE

 

• Phielemon Yang (Option B): Served as President of the 79th session of the UNGA (2024-25), the immediate predecessor to the 80th session.

 

• Dennis Francis (Option C): Served as President of the 78th session of the UNGA (2023-24).

 

• Volkan Bozkır (Option D): A former Turkish diplomat who served as President of the 75th session of the UNGA (2020-21).

question: 22 March 2025 marks which important regional day in Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar Statehood Day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 22 March is celebrated every year as Bihar Statehood Day (Bihar Diwas), commemorating the day in 1912 when Bihar was carved out as a separate province from the Bengal Presidency during British rule. (बिहार दिवस — 22 मार्च)

 

• The day is marked by various cultural and government programmes across Bihar, celebrating the state's history, heritage, and achievements, with the state government organising the annual 'Bihar Diwas' celebrations especially prominently in the state capital, Patna.

 

• Bihar Diwas celebrations often extend over multiple days and include exhibitions, cultural performances, and showcasing of the state's development initiatives.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bihar was earlier part of the Bengal Presidency; it became a separate province on 22 March 1912, and Odisha was later carved out of Bihar in 1936.

 

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000, becoming India's 28th state, with its formation marked annually as Jharkhand Sthapna Diwas.

 

• Patna, Bihar's capital, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, historically known as Pataliputra, capital of the Mauryan and Gupta empires.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar Brotherhood Day (Option B): Not a recognised official designation for 22 March.

 

• Bihar Reorganisation Day (Option C): Not the standard name used for this day; Bihar's major reorganisation (Jharkhand's creation) is separately marked on 15 November.

 

• Bihar Liberation Day (Option D): Not an official/recognised term for 22 March; the day is officially observed as Bihar Statehood Day (Bihar Diwas).

question: Which cabinet minister of Inda in June 2025 held bilateral talks with Dong Jun of China at the conclave of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) in the Chinese port city of Qingdao, with a focus on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raj Nath Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajnath Singh, the Union Defence Minister of India, held bilateral talks with his Chinese counterpart, Dong Jun (China's Defence Minister), on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Defence Ministers' conclave held in Qingdao, China, in June 2025. (राजनाथ सिंह — SCO सम्मेलन, चिंगदाओ, चीन)

 

• The talks focused on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), in the continuing context of India-China border disengagement and de-escalation efforts following the 2020 Galwan Valley standoff.

 

• The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) is a Eurasian political, economic and security grouping, of which India has been a full member since 2017.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SCO was founded in 2001 in Shanghai, China, and its permanent secretariat is based in Beijing; member states include China, Russia, India, Pakistan, and Central Asian nations among others.

 

• The Line of Actual Control (LAC) is the de facto border between India and China, distinct from the international boundary, and remains a subject of periodic diplomatic and military-level talks between the two countries.

 

• Rajnath Singh has been India's Defence Minister since 2019 and has represented India at several multilateral defence and security forums.

 

NOTE

 

• Manohar Lal (Option A): Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs / Power, not the Defence Minister who held these talks.

 

• Gajendra Singh Shekhawat (Option C): Union Minister for Culture and Tourism, unrelated to this defence-related engagement.

 

• Amit Shah (Option D): Union Home Minister, who handles internal security and home affairs, not this defence bilateral engagement with China.
